Spontaneous Communications: The public is encouraged to address the Parks & Recreation Commission on any matter listed on the
agenda or on any other matter within its jurisdiction. The Parks & Recreation Commission will hear public comments on items listed
on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote. The Parks & Recreation Commission will hear public comments
on matters not listed on the agenda during the Spontaneous Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
emergency or special circumstances exist.  The Parks & Recreation Commission may request from staff to investigate and/or
schedule certain matters for consideration at a future Commission or City Council meeting.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a Commission meeting
or other services offered by this City, please contact City Hall at (626) 430-2200. Assisted listening devices are available at this
meeting. Ask the Deputy City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet
can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with disabilities. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the
meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide
accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Staff reports are available for inspection at the office of the City Clerk, City Hall, 5050 N. Irwindale Avenue, during regular
business hours (8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday through Thursday).

  Code of Ethics

As City of Irwindale Parks & Recreation Commissioners, our fundamental duty is to serve the public good. We are
committed to the principle of an efficient and professional local government. We will be exemplary in obeying the letter
and spirit of Local, State and Federal laws and City policies affecting the operation of the government and in our private
life. We will be independent and impartial in our judgment and actions.

We will work for the common good of the City of Irwindale community and not for any private or personal interest. We
will endeavor to treat all people with respect and civility. We will commit to observe the highest standards of morality
and integrity, and to faithfully discharge the duties of our office regardless of personal consideration. We shall refrain
from abusive conduct, personal charges or verbal attacks upon the character or motives of others.

We will inform ourselves on public issues, listen attentively to public discussions before the body, and focus on the
business at hand. We will base our decisions on the merit and substance of that business. We will be fair and equitable
in all actions, claims or transactions. We shall not use our official position to influence government decisions in which
we have a financial interest or where we have a personal relationship that could present a conflict of interest, or create
a perception of a conflict of interest.

We shall not take advantage of services or opportunities for personal gain by virtue of our public office that are not
available to the public in general. We shall refrain from accepting gifts, favors or promises of future benefit that might
compromise our independence of judgment or action or give the appearance of being compromised.

We will behave in a manner that does not bring discredit or embarrassment to the City of Irwindale. We will be honest
in thought and deed in both our personal and official lives.

Ultimate responsibility for complying with this Code of Ethics rests with the individual elected official. In addition to any
other penalty as provided by law, violation of this Code of Ethics may be used as a basis for disciplinary action or censure
of a Commissioner.

These things we hereby pledge to do in the interest and purposes for which our government has been established.

This is the time set aside for members of the audience to speak on items not on this agenda. State law prohibits any
Commission discussion or action on such communications unless 1) the Commission by majority vote finds that a catastrophe

within the last five days. Since the Commission cannot participate (except as stated) it is requested that all such
communications be made in writing so as to be included on the next agenda for full discussion and action. If a member of the
audience feels he or she must proceed tonight, then each speaker will be limited to three minutes unless such time limits are

The Irwindale PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION met in special session at the above time
and place.

ROLL CALL:  Present: Commissioners Jason Hickman, Marguerite S. Lopez,
  Belen Zepeda; Vice Chair Paula Fraijo; Chair Dan Diaz

  Also present: Theresa Olivares, Assistant City Manager; Delfina
  Osterheim, Recreation Supervisor; Melissa Marez, Recreation
  Supervisor; Pedro Rodriguez Jr., Public Works Maintenance
  Supervisor; and Armando Hegdahl, Management Analyst

COMMISSION
REORGANIZATION

ANALYST HEGDAHL  Analyst Hegdahl explained the procedures for the reorganization of
  the Parks & Recreation Commission and opened the floor to
  nominations for the position of Chair.

COMMISSIONER DIAZ  Commissioner Diaz nominated Commissioner Fraijo.

ROLL CALL  There being no further nominations, Analyst Hegdahl closed the floor
  to nominations and, on a call for the vote, Commissioner Fraijo was
  unanimously appointed to the position of Chair.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Chair Fraijo resumed the meeting and opened the floor to nominations
  for the position of Vice Chair.

  Chair Fraijo nominated Commissioner Lopez

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Zepeda nominated Commissioner Hickman.
ZEPEDA

COMMISSIONER DIAZ  Commissioner Diaz also nominated Commissioner Hickman.

ROLL CALL  There being no further nominations, Chair Fraijo closed the floor to
  nominations.

  On roll call vote, the nomination of Commissioner Lopez as Vice
  Chair failed, with Commissioners Diaz, Hickman, Lopez, and Zepeda
  opposed; Chair Fraijo in favor.

  On roll call vote, Commissioner Hickman was unanimously
  appointed to the position of Vice Chair.

ITEM NO. 3A  IRWINDALE PARK IMPROVEMENTS PROJECT PHASE JIB; P-1005
IRWINDALE PARK
IMPROVEMENTS
PROJECT PHASE llB

ASSISTANT CITY  Assistant City Manager Olivares presented the report. She provided
MANAGER OLIVARES  background information on the bidding process for the selection of a
  contractor for the project, and explained why the Council has rejected
  all bids received. The project has since been split into three phases.
  The first phase (known as Phase Ill) will address the Memorial
  Garden, basketball court, bus and picnic shelters, bus turnout, exterior
  lighting, and the stairs for the Recreation Center. Contractors will be
  invited to bid on this phase in January, and staff is hopeful that the
  Council will award the contract in February.

  The other two phases are being designed by the project architect and
  will likely be constructed simultaneously. Additional details will be
  provided as they become available. The work is being coordinated in
  a manner that minimizes impacts to summer activities. Funding for the
  project has already been identified.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Chair Fraijo expressed her hope that the project will be completed in
  its entirety, as it had been shown to the commission, to which
  Assistant City Manager Olivares advised that staff has no intent to
  delay or cancel portions of the phases and spoke on efforts to
  appropriate the funding necessary for the project.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Lopez asked about the timing of the development of
LOPEZ  the proposed bus stop, to which Assistant City Manager Olivares
  indicated that staff will work with the project contractor to determine
  the construction schedule and determine which portions of the project
  would be prioritized. She also recognized that the specifications of the
  bus shelter would also need to be approved by the respective school
  district.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Responding to a request by Chair Fraijo, Assistant City Manager
  Olivares advised that additional details relating to the project would be
  provided at the February commission meeting.

RECREATION
DEPARTMENT UPDATE

RECREATION  Recreation Supervisor Osterheim provided the following update:
SUPERVISOR
OSTERHEIM  1) A trip to Mission Inn took place on December 14.
  2) Participants of the Winter Day Camp enjoyed the following
  outings: a trip to the movies on December 26 and a trip to Knott's
  Merry Farm on January 2.
  3) The Teen Club visited Magic Mountain on January 1.
  4) Registrations are being accepted for the trip to the Pantages
  Theatre to see the Frozen musical.
  5) The KidZone and Tiny Tots programs resumed this week.
  6) Registrations are being accepted for all winter classes.
  7) The gym floor will undergo its annual resurfacing tomorrow.
  Though the facility itself will be open, the basketball courts, locker
  rooms, and cardio room will be unavailable for the duration of the
  work.
  8) Thirty children preregistered for the Cookies with Santa event
  held on December 20. She thanked staff from the Library, Public
  Works, and Recreation departments for their collaboration in the
  successful event.
  9) The Christmas Spectacular and Mayor's Tree Lighting Ceremony,
  held on December 6, was enjoyed by all in attendance.

PUBLIC WORKS
DEPARTMENT UPDATE

SUPERVISOR  Supervisor Rodriguez reported on vandalism at the Skate Park and
RODRIGUEZ  advised that issues with the water fountain are being addressed. He
  also thanked his crew, city management, and the Recreation
  Department for their assistance in ensuring the success of the
  Christmas Spectacular.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Responding to a question from Chair Fraijo, Supervisor Rodriguez
  advised that the vandalism was reported to the Police. Chair Fraijo
  suggested that rewards be offered for those who provide information
  to the police that leads to the conviction of the vandal. Chair Fraijo
  also asked whether there are cameras at the Skate Park, to which
  Assistant City Manager Olivares replied that the cameras at the Skate
  Park are not functioning. She added that the city's IT Department has
  solicited informal bids for the installation of cameras at all city facilities.
  She also elaborated briefly on the high costs of camera equipment
  and video retention.

ASSISTANT CITY
MANAGER UPDATE

ASSISTANT CITY  Assistant City Manager Olivares spoke on the planned work for the
MANAGER OLIVARES  upcoming park improvement project, as well as the improvements
  already performed by the Public Works Department at the parks, and
  asked that the Commission determine whether its annual park walk-
  through would be necessary for this year, to which Chair Fraijo
  indicated that it would likely not be necessary.

  donations to the Christmas Spectacular, and thanked the Public
  Works Department for the wonderful decorations. Supervisor
  Osterheim also acknowledged the efforts and participation of the
  Police Department.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Lopez thanked the Recreation and Public Works
LOPEZ  Departments for their hard work in organizing the Christmas
  Spectacular.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Diaz spoke on his years serving on the Commission
DIAZ  and expressed his eagerness to continue serving for as long as he
  can.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Chair Fraijo thanked all the commissioners and staff for their support
  and for working to continuously improve the parks and recreational
